name: The Orchard

dates.altered: Altered 1913, when a flat-topped rectangular bay was added to the ground floor of the right cross wing.

quotes.text: House. 1899-1900 by C.F.A. Voysey for himself, altered 1913. Roughcast brick, stone and tile dressings. Green slate roof. Arts and Crafts Style. A simple rectangle on plan with the roof hipped over 2 gabled cross wings at ends. 2 storeys and attics. Slate paving up to entrance at right end of central range between cross wings. Round arch to recessed porch.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, opening paragraph (List Entry Number 1348234).

quotes.text: Mullioned windows with stone surrounds, leaded lights. To left of entrance 3 lights with 4 lights above on first floor. Continuous tile dripmould over ground floor.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, entrance front; the extracted span continues 'Deep'.

quotes.text: Large roughcast axial stack with a tile coped triangulated cap and terracotta pots to left of centre. Similar stacks on outer slopes of cross wings.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, entrance front, second span.

quotes.text: Each cross wing has a 4 light window on each floor. Continuous tile drip mould over ground floor and over first floor in wings, triple ventilation slits in gables with moulded trim.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, garden front.

quotes.text: Interior: slate paved hall with tiled fireplace and staircase enclosed by simple vertical slats, elsewhere tiled and cast iron chimneypieces, low picture rails, wrought iron hinges and knobs to doors.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details section, interior, above the bibliography.

measurements.name: cross_wing_count
measurements.note: A simple rectangle in plan with the roof hipped over two gabled cross wings -- the plainest statement of an Arts and Crafts massing rule anywhere in this cluster's evidence.

measurements.name: cross_wing_window_light_count
measurements.as_printed: a 4 light window on each floor

measurements.name: entrance_front_window_light_count
measurements.as_printed: 3 lights with 4 lights above on first floor
measurements.note: Two figures for the two floors of one bay; no single value is parsed. The upper window is wider than the lower, which is the reverse of the classical rule and is worth having on record.

note: Tranche 3, British picturesque and Arts and Crafts cluster, 5 Sep 2026. Added as a new exemplar of `arts-and-crafts-british`: Voysey's own house, and the only entry in the cluster whose Details text names the style as the corpus does -- 'Arts and Crafts Style'. Its low picture rails are the register recording the thing the node's prose describes as design aimed at the body rather than the eye. `id` carries the place name because the corpus already holds `the-orchard-james-l-breese-house`, a different building of the same name in New York.
